```{r set_options, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.align = "center"
)
```

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(phylograftR)
```

Grafting can be constrained by **species attributes** (e.g., a trait, a biogeographic range) described by **stochastic character maps** of the backbone phylogeny, called `simmap` in `phytools`.
This tutorial explains how to **prepare these maps from your own tip data**, and which object to provide to the grafting functions in each case:

1. **A single `simmap`**: one history of the attribute along the branches of the backbone.
2. **A `multiSimmap`**: a set of histories of the **same** attribute (e.g., 100 maps), which accounts for the **uncertainty** in the reconstruction of the ancestral states.
3. **A list of `multiSimmap`s**: one set of maps **per attribute**, to combine several traits (or a trait and biogeographic ranges).

We use the R package [`deepSTRAPP`](https://github.com/MaelDore/deepSTRAPP), which fits the **evolutionary models** on the tip data, selects the best one, and simulates the stochastic maps in a **single call**: `deepSTRAPP::prepare_trait_data()`.
It handles **categorical traits**, **biogeographic ranges** (through `BioGeoBEARS`) and **continuous traits**.

**Why `deepSTRAPP` rather than `phytools::make.simmap()` alone?**

- **Model comparison and selection are automatic.** `phytools::make.simmap()` fits the single model you ask for (e.g., `"ARD"`) and simulates the maps under it: choosing the model is up to you. `prepare_trait_data()` **fits all the candidate models, compares them with their AICc, selects the best one** and simulates the maps under it, and returns the table of the comparison.
- **One call for all the types of attributes**: categorical traits, biogeographic ranges and continuous traits follow the same logic, with the same arguments.
- **For biogeographic ranges, it embeds the whole machinery of `BioGeoBEARS`**: preparation of the input files, fit and comparison of the models (`DEC`, `DIVALIKE`, `BAYAREALIKE`, with or without `+J`), **biogeographic stochastic mapping**, and the **conversion of the outputs of `BioGeoBEARS` (tables of cladogenetic and anagenetic events) into `simmap`s**, which `BioGeoBEARS` does not provide.
- It also returns the posterior probabilities of the states at the nodes, and the maps are reproducible with a `seed`.

Using `deepSTRAPP` is a recommendation, not a requirement: any `simmap` or `multiSimmap` of the backbone can be used, for instance maps built directly with `phytools::make.simmap()` when you have already chosen your model.

**The code that runs `deepSTRAPP` and `BioGeoBEARS` is shown but not run here** (these packages are only suggested, and the runs can be long).
The **results** are loaded from datasets shipped with `phylograftR`: they were produced with this code (see `data-raw/toy_prepare_trait_data.R` in the source of the package).

| Attribute | `trait_data_type` | Models available (default) | Output of `prepare_trait_data()` to use | Provide to the grafting functions |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| Categorical trait | `"categorical"` | `"ER"`, `"SYM"`, `"ARD"`, `"meristic"`, `"matrix"` (`"ARD"`) | `$simmaps` | `simmap` / `multiSimmap` |
| Biogeographic ranges | `"biogeographic"` | `"DEC"`, `"DEC+J"`, `"DIVALIKE"`, `"DIVALIKE+J"`, `"BAYAREALIKE"`, `"BAYAREALIKE+J"` (`"DEC"`) | `$simmaps` | `simmap` / `multiSimmap` |
| Continuous trait | `"continuous"` | `"BM"`, `"OU"`, `"EB"`, ... (`"BM"`) | `$contMaps` | **discretize first**: see `vignette("continuous_data")` |

## 0/ Toy data

We use the toy backbone and the **tip data of three attributes**: a color (three states), an elevation (two states) and a biogeographic range.
The tip data are held in a `data.frame` with one row per tip.

```{r data}
# ------ Toy data ------ #

data(toy_backbone)
data(toy_tip_data)
data(toy_multiSimmap)
data(toy_multiSimmap_elevation)
data(toy_multiSimmap_ranges)

# Tip data of the three attributes
head(toy_tip_data)
lapply(toy_tip_data, table)
```

`deepSTRAPP::prepare_trait_data()` needs the tip data of one attribute as a **named vector**, with names that match the tip labels of the phylogeny (`phylo$tip.label`):

```{r tip_vectors}
# ------ Named vectors of tip data ------ #

tip_colors <- setNames(toy_tip_data$color, row.names(toy_tip_data))
tip_elevations <- setNames(toy_tip_data$elevation, row.names(toy_tip_data))
tip_ranges <- setNames(toy_tip_data$range, row.names(toy_tip_data))

# The names are the tip labels of the backbone
all(names(tip_colors) == toy_backbone$tip.label)
```

```{r colors}
# ------ Colors of the states ------ #

color_states <- c(blue = "dodgerblue", green = "limegreen", red = "firebrick")
```

## 1/ Infer maps of a categorical trait with deepSTRAPP

The call below **fits three models of evolution of the color, compares them, selects automatically the one with the lowest AICc**, and simulates stochastic maps conditioned on the tip data and on the best model.
With `phytools::make.simmap()`, you would have to fit each model, compare them and choose the best one yourself before simulating the maps.

```{r deepSTRAPP_color, eval = FALSE}
# ------ Not run: build the maps of the color with deepSTRAPP ------ #

color_data <- deepSTRAPP::prepare_trait_data(tip_data = tip_colors, # Named vector of tip states
                                             trait_data_type = "categorical",
                                             phylo = toy_backbone, # Time-calibrated phylogeny
                                             evolutionary_models = c("ER", "SYM", "ARD"), # Models to compare. Default is "ARD"
                                             seed = 1234, # For reproducibility
                                             nb_simulations = 100, # Number of stochastic maps
                                             return_simmaps = TRUE, # Needed to get the maps
                                             return_model_selection_df = TRUE, # Needed to get the comparison of models
                                             plot_map = FALSE, plot_overlay = FALSE)

# Comparison of the models
color_data$model_selection_df

# The stochastic maps: a multiSimmap of 100 maps
my_multiSimmap <- color_data$simmaps
```

The main arguments are:

- `evolutionary_models`: the models to compare (see the table above). The model with the lowest AICc is used to simulate the maps. A **custom matrix of transitions** (`Q_matrix`) can be used with the model `"matrix"`, for instance to forbid some transitions between states (e.g., an ordered trait).
- `nb_simulations`: the **number of maps**. `deepSTRAPP` recommends at least 100 maps, and warns if fewer are requested.
- `return_simmaps = TRUE`: **the maps are only returned in `$simmaps` if you ask for them**. By default, `prepare_trait_data()` only returns the summaries that `deepSTRAPP` needs for its own workflow (e.g., `$densityMaps`).
- `seed`: to reproduce the maps.

The maps are **conditioned on the tip data**: the tips are always in the states you provided, and the maps only differ in the internal branches.
The maps shipped with `phylograftR` are the **first 10 of 100 maps** simulated with this code. 10 maps are enough for illustration, but **actual analyses should use more (100 or more)**.

## 2/ Use a single map: `simmap`

A **single `simmap`** is one possible history of the trait: take **one map** of the output.
It is the simplest input of `simmap` for the grafting functions, and it is enough to explore the grafting with constraints.

```{r single_simmap, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 6, out.width = "60%"}
# ------ One simmap ------ #

# Extract one map (with [[ ]]): an object of class "simmap"
my_simmap <- toy_multiSimmap[[1]]
class(my_simmap)

# Time spent in each state (sum on all branches)
round(colSums(my_simmap$mapped.edge) / sum(my_simmap$mapped.edge), 2)

# The tips are in the states of the tip data
all(phytools::getStates(my_simmap, type = "tips")[names(tip_colors)] == tip_colors)

# Plot the map
phytools::plotSimmap(my_simmap, colors = color_states, fsize = 0.7, ftype = "i", lwd = 2)
```

A single map is **one hypothesis among many** about where the states changed along the branches.
Grafting with it treats this history as known, so the **uncertainty on the ancestral states is ignored**.

## 3/ Use several maps: `multiSimmap`

The **full output** `$simmaps` is a `multiSimmap`: a set of maps of the same trait, used as **alternative hypotheses** about its evolution.
Provide it as `simmap` to the grafting functions: each map is then used for the grafting, and the uncertainty on the history of the trait is **propagated to the grafted phylogenies**.

```{r multiSimmap}
# ------ A multiSimmap ------ #

class(toy_multiSimmap)
length(toy_multiSimmap)

# All the maps are in the same states
unique(unlist(lapply(toy_multiSimmap, function (x) colnames(x$mapped.edge))))
```

The maps share the same tip states, but differ in the **internal branches**:

```{r multiSimmap_plot, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 4.5, out.width = "100%"}
# ------ Compare three maps ------ #

par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(0.5, 0.5, 2, 0.5))
for (i in 1:3)
{
  phytools::plotSimmap(toy_multiSimmap[[i]], colors = color_states, fsize = 0.5, ftype = "i", lwd = 2)
  title(paste("Map", i), line = -1, cex.main = 1)
}
par(mfrow = c(1, 1), mar = c(5.1, 4.1, 4.1, 2.1))
```

The **posterior probabilities of each state at the internal nodes**, computed over the maps, summarize this uncertainty:

```{r multiSimmap_pies, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 6, out.width = "60%"}
# ------ Posterior probability of the states at the nodes ------ #

node_probs <- phytools::describe.simmap(toy_multiSimmap, plot = FALSE)$ace

phytools::plotTree(toy_backbone, ftype = "i", fsize = 0.6, lwd = 1)
ape::nodelabels(pie = node_probs, piecol = color_states[colnames(node_probs)], cex = 0.5)
```

The more maps, the more precise the probabilities.
Note that the **number of maps and the number of simulations multiply**: with `P` maps and `N` simulations per map, `P x N` grafted phylogenies are produced (see `vignette("graft_missing_taxa")`).

## 4/ Combine several traits: list of `multiSimmap`s

To use **several attributes at once** as constraints, prepare the maps of **each attribute separately** (the attributes are modelled independently), and combine them in a **list with one element per attribute**.
We prepare the maps of the elevation as for the color:

```{r deepSTRAPP_elevation, eval = FALSE}
# ------ Not run: build the maps of the elevation with deepSTRAPP ------ #

elevation_data <- deepSTRAPP::prepare_trait_data(tip_data = tip_elevations,
                                                 trait_data_type = "categorical",
                                                 phylo = toy_backbone,
                                                 evolutionary_models = c("ER", "ARD"),
                                                 seed = 2345,
                                                 nb_simulations = 100, # The same number of maps as for the color
                                                 return_simmaps = TRUE,
                                                 plot_map = FALSE, plot_overlay = FALSE)

my_multiSimmap_elevation <- elevation_data$simmaps
```

The list is named after the traits, and **all the traits must have the same number of maps**: the maps are **paired** (map 1 of each trait is used together, then map 2 of each trait, and so on).

```{r two_traits}
# ------ List of multiSimmaps: one element per trait ------ #

maps_two_traits <- list(color = toy_multiSimmap, elevation = toy_multiSimmap_elevation)

# Number of maps per trait: must be the same
sapply(maps_two_traits, length)

# States of each trait
lapply(maps_two_traits, function (x) colnames(x[[1]]$mapped.edge))
```

```{r two_traits_plot, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 5.5, out.width = "100%"}
# ------ Map 1 of each trait ------ #

elevation_states <- c(high = "darkorange", low = "steelblue")

par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(0.5, 0.5, 2, 0.5))
phytools::plotSimmap(toy_multiSimmap[[1]], colors = color_states, fsize = 0.55, ftype = "i", lwd = 2)
title("Color: map 1", line = -1, cex.main = 1)
phytools::plotSimmap(toy_multiSimmap_elevation[[1]], colors = elevation_states, fsize = 0.55, ftype = "i", lwd = 2)
title("Elevation: map 1", line = -1, cex.main = 1)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1), mar = c(5.1, 4.1, 4.1, 2.1))
```

The list is provided as `simmap`, and the **allowed states** are then given as a list with one element per trait.
The grafting with several traits is detailed in `vignette("multiple_traits")`.
A list of single `simmap`s (one map per trait) works in the same way. The two cannot be mixed: **a trait with a single `simmap` and another with a `multiSimmap` is refused**.

## 5/ Infer maps of biogeographic ranges with BioGeoBEARS

For **biogeographic ranges**, `deepSTRAPP::prepare_trait_data()` embeds **the whole machinery of the [`BioGeoBEARS`](https://github.com/nmatzke/BioGeoBEARS) framework** in a single call:

1. it prepares the **input files** of `BioGeoBEARS` from your phylogeny and your tip ranges;
2. it **fits the models** you ask for, and **selects the best one** by AICc (the models with a `+J` parameter are fit starting from the estimates of the corresponding model without `J`);
3. it runs the **biogeographic stochastic mapping** (BSM) under the best model, which simulates histories of the ranges as **tables of cladogenetic events** (at the nodes) and **anagenetic events** (along the branches);
4. it **converts these tables of events into `simmap`s**, the format used by `phylograftR`. This step is not provided by `BioGeoBEARS`, and is tedious to do by hand.

`BioGeoBEARS` is not on CRAN and must be installed manually (`remotes::install_github("nmatzke/BioGeoBEARS")`).

The tip data are the ranges of the tips, **coded as in `BioGeoBEARS`**: one capital letter per area, and the letters of a multi-area range in alphabetical order (e.g., `"A"`, `"AB"`).
Alternatively, they can be provided as a `matrix` or `data.frame` of presence (1) / absence (0), with one column per area and one row per taxon.

```{r deepSTRAPP_ranges, eval = FALSE}
# ------ Not run: build the maps of the ranges with deepSTRAPP and BioGeoBEARS ------ #

range_data <- deepSTRAPP::prepare_trait_data(tip_data = tip_ranges, # Named vector of ranges (or binary matrix)
                                             trait_data_type = "biogeographic",
                                             phylo = toy_backbone,
                                             evolutionary_models = "DEC", # Models to compare, e.g., c("DEC", "DEC+J", "DIVALIKE", "DIVALIKE+J")
                                             max_range_size = 2, # Maximum number of areas in a range
                                             BioGeoBEARS_directory_path = "./BioGeoBEARS_files/", # Directory for input/output files
                                             keep_BioGeoBEARS_files = FALSE,
                                             nb_cores = 1,
                                             seed = 3456,
                                             nb_simulations = 100,
                                             return_simmaps = TRUE,
                                             return_model_selection_df = TRUE,
                                             return_BSM = FALSE, # TRUE to also get the tables of events
                                             plot_map = FALSE, plot_overlay = FALSE)

# Comparison of the models
range_data$model_selection_df

# The stochastic maps of ranges, converted from the BSM events: a multiSimmap of 100 maps
my_multiSimmap_ranges <- range_data$simmaps
```

The main arguments specific to ranges are:

- `evolutionary_models`: the `BioGeoBEARS` models to compare, **fit and selected automatically**. The `+J` models add jump dispersal (founder-event speciation).
- `return_BSM = TRUE`: also returns the **tables of cladogenetic and anagenetic events** of each simulation, from which the maps are built (`$BSM_output`).
- `max_range_size`: the **maximum number of areas** in a range. It limits the number of ranges considered, so the computation time.
- `BioGeoBEARS_directory_path`: the directory where the input and output files of `BioGeoBEARS` are written (and kept if `keep_BioGeoBEARS_files = TRUE`).
- `nb_cores`: the number of cores used for the runs of `BioGeoBEARS`.

The output `$simmaps` is a `multiSimmap`, as for a categorical trait, in which the **states are the ranges**.

```{r ranges_check}
# ------ Maps of ranges ------ #

class(toy_multiSimmap_ranges)
length(toy_multiSimmap_ranges)

# Ranges found in the maps
all_ranges <- sort(unique(unlist(lapply(toy_multiSimmap_ranges, function (x) colnames(x$mapped.edge)))))
all_ranges

# Ranges of the tips
sort(unique(tip_ranges))
```

The ranges of the maps include the ranges of the tips, and may include **ranges that are only found along internal branches**, as ancestors can have ranges that no tip has.
Keep it in mind when you choose the **allowed ranges** of the missing taxa: they must be ranges found in the maps, unless `treat_states_as_ranges = TRUE` is used to match areas (see `vignette("biogeographic_data")`).

```{r ranges_plot, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 5.5, out.width = "100%"}
# ------ Compare two maps of ranges ------ #

# One color per range
range_colors <- setNames(grDevices::hcl.colors(length(all_ranges), palette = "Dynamic"), all_ranges)

par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(0.5, 0.5, 2, 0.5))
for (i in 1:2)
{
  phytools::plotSimmap(toy_multiSimmap_ranges[[i]], colors = range_colors, fsize = 0.55, ftype = "i", lwd = 2)
  title(paste("Map", i), line = -1, cex.main = 1)
}
par(mfrow = c(1, 1), mar = c(5.1, 4.1, 4.1, 2.1))
```

```{r ranges_legend, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 1.2, out.width = "70%"}
# ------ Legend ------ #

par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
plot.new()
legend("center", legend = names(range_colors), fill = range_colors, horiz = TRUE, bty = "n", title = "Range")
par(mar = c(5.1, 4.1, 4.1, 2.1))
```

In the maps, the **changes of range happen along the branches** (anagenetic changes: dispersal or local extinction) and **at the nodes** (cladogenetic events, e.g., vicariance), where a descendant branch starts in a range different from the one of its parent.

## 6/ Continuous traits

For a **continuous trait**, `deepSTRAPP::prepare_trait_data(trait_data_type = "continuous")` returns a `contMap` (`$contMap`) and, with `run_stochastic_maps = TRUE`, a **list of `contMap`s** (`$contMaps`), which are **not** stochastic character maps.
They must be **discretized into states** with `phylograftR::convert_contMap_to_simmap()` before they can constrain the grafting.
Do **not** discretize the tip values before the reconstruction: the discretization is applied on the continuous reconstruction.
The full procedure, and the reasons for it, are detailed in `vignette("continuous_data")`.

## 7/ Common pitfalls

**Only an object of class `multiSimmap` is read as a set of maps of one trait.**
A plain `list` of `simmap`s is read as **one map per trait**.
Several R operations return a plain `list` and drop the class `multiSimmap`, such as `lapply()` or `unclass()`, whereas `[` (subset), `c()` and `rev()` keep it.
The extraction of one map with `[[` returns a `simmap`, as expected.

```{r pitfall_class}
# ------ Which operations keep the class multiSimmap? ------ #

data.frame(Operation = c("Original", "Subset: x[1:3]", "One map: x[[1]]", "Concatenate: c(x, x)", "lapply(x, identity)", "unclass(x)"),
           Class = sapply(list(toy_multiSimmap, toy_multiSimmap[1:3], toy_multiSimmap[[1]], c(toy_multiSimmap, toy_multiSimmap),
                               lapply(toy_multiSimmap, identity), unclass(toy_multiSimmap)),
                          function (x) paste(class(x), collapse = ", ")))
```

If the class is lost, the maps are read as the maps of **as many traits as maps**.
Without any constraint, **no error is raised**: the plan shows a **single map**, whereas the `multiSimmap` has 10:

```{r pitfall_plan}
# ------ A plain list is read as the maps of 10 traits ------ #

data(toy_missing_taxa_list)

# Plain list: class lost
plain_list <- lapply(toy_multiSimmap, identity)

# Grafting plan with the multiSimmap: 10 maps
plan_multi <- check_grafting_plan(phy = toy_backbone, missing_taxa_list = toy_missing_taxa_list,
                                  simmap = toy_multiSimmap, verbose = FALSE)
attr(plan_multi, "n_maps")

# Grafting plan with the plain list: 1 map of 10 traits
plan_plain <- check_grafting_plan(phy = toy_backbone, missing_taxa_list = toy_missing_taxa_list,
                                  simmap = plain_list, verbose = FALSE)
attr(plan_plain, "n_maps")
```

As soon as allowed states are provided as a single vector, the function **stops** and tells you that the maps of 10 traits are used:

```{r pitfall_error, error = TRUE}
# ------ Error with allowed states ------ #

check_grafting_plan(phy = toy_backbone, missing_taxa_list = toy_missing_taxa_list,
                    simmap = plain_list, allowed_states = c("blue", "green"), verbose = FALSE)
```

To restore the class, set it back, and check the number of maps with `check_grafting_plan()`:

```{r pitfall_fix}
# ------ Restore the class ------ #

class(plain_list) <- c("multiSimmap", "multiPhylo")
plan_fixed <- check_grafting_plan(phy = toy_backbone, missing_taxa_list = toy_missing_taxa_list,
                                  simmap = plain_list, verbose = FALSE)
attr(plan_fixed, "n_maps")
```

**All the traits must have the same number of maps** (maps are paired across traits), and a `simmap` cannot be mixed with a `multiSimmap`:

```{r pitfall_n_maps, error = TRUE}
# ------ Different numbers of maps among traits ------ #

check_grafting_plan(phy = toy_backbone, missing_taxa_list = toy_missing_taxa_list,
                    simmap = list(color = toy_multiSimmap, elevation = toy_multiSimmap_elevation[1:5]),
                    verbose = FALSE)
```

Other points to keep in mind:

- **All the maps must have the same tips, topology and branch lengths as the backbone** used for grafting. If you prune or rescale the phylogeny after building the maps, **rebuild the maps** on the final phylogeny.
- The **allowed states** of the missing taxa must be states found in the maps (or areas contained in the ranges of the maps, with `treat_states_as_ranges = TRUE`). See *Section 6* in `vignette("format_inputs")` for the allowed states.
- The maps are **hypotheses conditioned on the tip data you provide**: the quality of the grafting constraint depends on the quality of the tip data and on the fit of the evolutionary model.

## Next steps

- Use the maps to constrain the grafting: see `vignette("main_workflow")` for a full example with one trait, `vignette("multiple_traits")` for several traits, and `vignette("biogeographic_data")` for ranges.
- Use a continuous trait: see `vignette("continuous_data")`.
- For a thorough presentation of the models and of the options of `prepare_trait_data()`, see the vignettes of the `deepSTRAPP` package.
